text: Gold fell about 3.4% to near $3,884, its lowest in about a year, as markets still expect the Fed to raise rates in December.
Silver dropped about 6% to $48.90, an 11-month low, lifting the gold/silver ratio to about 79; SLV closed down 5.7% at $44.60.
Gold miners fell harder than gold: GDX lost 5.2% to $77.09 and GDXJ 5.9% to $94.97.

The Nasdaq fell 2.9% and the S&P 500 1.8%, its worst day since June, after Intel dropped about 29% and Amazon missed estimates. The Nasdaq-100 entered a correction; QQQ fell 3.5% and TQQQ about 10.5%.
The VIX volatility gauge jumped about 13% to 19.42.
Treasury yields fell as money moved into bonds: the 10-year to about 4.94% and the 2-year to about 4.60%.
Brent settled up 2.4% at $117.64, its highest since late April, on fears the Iran war could escalate after the midterms.
Bitcoin slipped to about $77,300 after dipping near $76,200 on the Binance hack.
